2.role: tip + the one casual app mention
2.asset: sheet music, notebook, open case, tuner on a stand — no app UI

A: intonation is SO important you guys, and it's really easy to not notice
check your notes against a drone or a tuner while you practice! i use this app called {app}, it tells me exactly which notes i got wrong
B: your open strings are a free tuner and nobody uses them 🥹
3rd finger in first position is an octave above the string below — check it every time. i also run {app} while i practice so it flags the ones i miss
C: turn the vibrato OFF when you're checking intonation
vibrato hides a flat note from you AND from a tuner. i practice the passage plain first, then check it with {app} before adding it back
D: record yourself. you will be humbled 😭
your ears genuinely lie to you while you're playing. voice memos work fine — i use {app} because it marks the bits that went wrong so i don't have to relisten
E: play QUIETER when something isn't in tune
you hear so much more at a soft dynamic, it's kind of magic. that plus a drone fixed more for me than any amount of scales (i check mine with {app} now)
F: stop starting from the top every single time!!
your first 8 bars are amazing and your ending is a mess, be honest 🥲 pick the bar that's actually broken. {app} tells me which one that is if i can't tell
G: private teachers are SO expensive and i need you to know that's okay!!
you can get really far on your own i promise 🥹 free stuff first — a tuner, a drone track, and recording yourself. i also use this app called {app} because it tells me exactly which notes i got wrong
H: there were no violin teachers near me and i almost didn't start 😭
so glad i did anyway!! it's just youtube, a metronome and {app} for me — it listens while i play and catches the notes i can't hear are off. genuinely so doable on your own 💕

3.role: ear and intonation — no app mention
3.asset: fingerboard, strings, tuner, hand in position

A: hear the note in your head BEFORE you put the finger down ✨
sounds fake but it works. if you don't know what you're aiming for you're just guessing and hoping
B: a perfect 5th rings when it's in tune 🎻
if you hear a little wobble in the sound, that's the two notes fighting each other. adjust until the wobble disappears
C: practise with a drone!! it's so humbling but so good
hold a note against it and let it settle. you'll start hearing the problem before the tuner does
D: you're using your eyes for something your ears are supposed to do. it feels awful for two weeks and then your ear takes over
E: play slow enough that you can actually hear each note land
if it's too fast to hear, it's too fast to fix. speed is the last thing you add, not the first
F: sing the phrase before you play it
you'll be shocked how much cleaner it comes out. your fingers follow your ear, not the other way round

4.role: bow, vibrato, posture — no app mention
4.asset: bow hold, right arm mid-stroke, shoulder and chin frame

A: a straight bow isn't a straight arm 🤯
your hand actually travels in a slight curve — out towards the tip, back in towards the frog. that's what keeps the bow parallel to the bridge
B: loudness comes from bow SPEED, not pressure
pressing harder just chokes the string. move faster and a little closer to the bridge instead
C: your contact point changes the whole sound 🎻
near the bridge = loud and bright, near the fingerboard = soft and airy. pick one on purpose instead of drifting
D: if your thumb is squeezing, your vibrato is dead ✨
it's the number one thing killing it. you should be able to wiggle your thumb loose mid-note — if you can't, you're gripping
E: slow wide vibrato first, speed comes later 🥹
metronome at 60, two swings per beat. it narrows on its own as it speeds up, so don't chase fast
F: long tones on one open string. that's the whole warmup.
whole bow, as slow as you can hold it steady. deeply boring, fixes more than any étude

5.asset: music stand, practice space, notebook, metronome

A: decide the one thing you're fixing before you open the case. wandering practice just rehearses your mistakes
B: practise the hard bar, not the whole piece 🥹
four bars, fifty times, slowly. that's a real session — running it top to bottom is just performing at yourself
C: slow, then medium, then fast. don't skip the middle one.
if it falls apart at tempo you skipped a step. going back down feels like losing and it really isn't
D: a little every day beats one long weekend session 🎻
your hands learn overnight, genuinely. fifteen minutes daily will outrun two hours on a sunday
E: picking something way too hard feels ambitious and mostly teaches you tension. the piece one step up is the one that makes you better
F: stop the second you feel your hand tense up
tension is the fastest way to build a habit you'll spend a year undoing. shake it out, breathe, start again
